key_insight: For geometry-aware hemodynamic surrogates, active learning and finite-element physical consistency are more effective during fine-tuning than during early training.
engineering_relevance: The framework supports scalable prediction of patient-specific aortic velocity and pressure fields toward real-time cardiovascular assessment.
method: Generate physiologically consistent CFD data from SynthAorta geometries using automatic boundary-condition adjustment.
Represent anatomies as displacement fields on a shared reference geometry and train Graph U-Net and Transformer U-Net surrogates.
Fine-tune using gradient- or subspace-based active learning and differentiable finite-element residual constraints.
evidence_signal: Peak-systolic evaluations show little early-training benefit from active learning, improved fine-tuning performance, and out-of-distribution limitations tied primarily to geometric coverage.
watch_item: Generalization remains limited by the anatomical shapes supported by the geometry parametrization; architecture changes alone may not resolve this.
paper_title: Synthetic Dataset Generation, Physical Consistency and Active Learning for Shape-Informed Surrogate Modeling of Hemodynamics
